clue.text: Lad visited by doctor with answer — avoid fish

indicators.note: a lad visited by callers has them inside his house, so these letters go within the word for lad

parts.note: a lad is a boy
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor
to duck something is to dodge or avoid it

explanation.surface: A young man gets a house call from his GP and is told to keep off fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two visitors; the house call reading hides that DUCK is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay duck is a small lizardfish of South Asian waters, usually eaten dried and salted.

clue.text: Simple line crossed by criminal

indicators.note: the line is crossed, held within, by the word for criminal

parts.note: bad means wicked or criminal

explanation.surface: A plain line drawn across by a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A bald statement is plain and unadorned, so simple.

clue.text: Deal badly with worker, taken in by awkward smile

indicators.note: the worker is taken inside the scrambled letters
awkward means clumsy and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: A worker gets mistreated, fooled by a clumsy grin.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker looks like the victim, but is the piece 'taken in by' the letters that 'awkward' rearranges into MISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishandle is to manage or treat something badly.

clue.text: Subtle quality of a second artist on the rise

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter's reputation climbing, with a fine quality, in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns A MO RA upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive smell, and figuratively a subtle pervasive quality or air.

clue.text: Remove underwear and ask for information after operation

definitions.meaning: jokingly, to ... is to take off one's briefs
to question someone after a mission

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to undress before questioning someone after surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Debriefing is the formal questioning of agents or soldiers once a mission ends; the first sense is a playful coinage.

clue.text: 7 Down may be encouragement I love

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A farewell may be a cheery boost from someone in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 Down is ADIEU; both are ways to say goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, as adieu is a French one.

clue.text: Brandy may see study going west!

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so the word for study runs right to left

parts.note: to cram is to study hard before an exam

explanation.surface: A brandy bottle might watch someone's studies come to nothing, going west.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a French spirit distilled from grape skins and pips left after pressing, a kind of brandy.

clue.text: All the best gold rings perish

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the gold goes around the word for perish

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: A farewell wish next to golden rings that will perish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewell phrases; adieu is the French goodbye, commending one to God.

clue.text: Keep a cash supply, saving time for one who doesn't like spending

indicators.note: saving is read as keeping safe within, so the time letter sits inside
read as supple, bending, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to hold a cash reserve and save time, aimed at a miser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' rearranges KEEP A CASH around T; it looks like a noun but works as the adjective supple.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who avoids paying out.

clue.text: The girl's in a depression, being a fan

indicators.note: in places the girl's letters inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
her is the possessive, the girl's

explanation.surface: A girl is down in the dumps because she is a supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause, like a fan.

clue.text: What a cowboy needs from girl with nothing

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cowboy's requirements are teased as coming from a girl with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher's rope with a running noose is standard equipment for catching cattle.

clue.text: Poor souls waiting at the hole in the wall?

definitions.text: Poor souls waiting at the hole in the wall?

parts.words: Poor souls waiting at the hole in the wall?
parts.note: a hole in the wall is a cash machine; bread is slang for money, and a queue for it is a line, while the phrase also names the threshold of poverty

explanation.surface: Hard-up people queue at a cash machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole in the wall' is British slang for an ATM; the old soup-kitchen queue, the line for bread, gives the phrase for the poverty level.
explanation.definitionFit: Those on the poverty threshold are said to live on it, recalling queues for free food.

clue.text: After wine, political wings will accept that is arrogant

indicators.note: the second part is placed after the wine in the answer

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the wings enclose the abbreviation for that is

parts.note: the left and right wings, abbreviated L and R
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: After a drink, both ends of the political spectrum accept something haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand and disdainful, showing a haughty lack of proper concern.

clue.text: Supply crack on base

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it, so the crack sits after the base

parts.note: E is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics
a crack is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: A command to provide a joke about a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply someone with what they need is to fit them out or provide for them.

clue.text: Mostly produce a favourable reaction on a Spanish flower producer

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to impress is to make a good impression
a flower is a river, something that flows; rio is Spanish for river

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a Spanish flower growing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and stages concerts or shows, so produces them.

clue.text: Scarpered from crazed force holding enemy back

indicators.note: the pieces around it hold the reversed enemy in their grip

parts.note: crazed means mad
F is the physics abbreviation for force

indicators.note: back says the word for enemy is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: Someone fled from a frenzied army that was keeping the enemy at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is only a link; 'back' turns the enemy round, and 'holding' puts the result between crazed and force.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for running away, as is to make off.

clue.text: No money around the middle of July for luxury

parts.note: O looks like zero, no

indicators.note: the money goes around the central letters

parts.note: pence are British coins, money

indicators.note: the middle of takes the central letters of July

explanation.surface: No cash left by mid-July for treats.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is lavish wealth and luxuriousness.

clue.text: Needle may give bobble regularly with crushed silk

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of the word bobble
crushed fabric is crumpled out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a knitting needle producing a bobble with crumpled silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks OBE from bobble; 'crushed' turns SILK into LISK.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's Needle in London is a famous obelisk, a tall tapering stone pillar.

clue.text: Improvised setter's cue on origin of universe

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so setter's is I'M, I am
a prompt is a cue, as given to an actor

indicators.note: origin of takes the first letter of universe

explanation.surface: A setter's cue about the start of the cosmos was made up on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done without preparation, off the cuff.

clue.text: Bank said to have responsibility for animal

indicators.note: said signals the word for bank is taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: a bank of seats or keys is a row
the buck is responsibility, as in 'the buck stops here'

explanation.surface: A bank is claimed to be in charge of some creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The roebuck is the male of the roe deer, a small European deer.

clue.text: Rapper's critic?

parts.note: one who knocks something criticises it; a door rapper is the metal fitting, and a rap critic would knock rapping

explanation.surface: Someone who criticises a rap artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a fault-finder and the device that raps on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock is to criticise, and a door's metal rapper bears the same name.

clue.text: Area of potential conflict sees sexy garments making a comeback

parts.note: hot is slang for sexy

indicators.note: coming back means running backwards, so the garments are read right to left

parts.note: tops are garments worn on the upper body

explanation.surface: A trouble zone sees racy clothes back in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns TOPS into SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashpoint region where fighting may break out is called this, as is any lively place.

clue.text: Journalist understood this might cut

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often disparagingly
saw means understood, as in 'I saw what you meant'

explanation.surface: A reporter grasped that this piece might get cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting metal.

clue.text: Functional out of uniform fur

indicators.note: out of means without, so the letter for uniform is dropped

parts.note: functional means usable
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Practical clothing, once out of uniform, means fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the dark pelt of a small Asian marten, prized by furriers.

clue.text: Food firm trapped in embargo

indicators.note: the firm is held inside the embargo word

parts.note: an embargo is a ban
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A food company caught by a trade embargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork, a familiar food.

clue.text: Justification for affair?

definitions.meaning: an ... can mean a reason or grounds, as in 'no ... to complain'
an event or function, an affair

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for an excuse for an extramarital fling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: grounds for doing something, and a social event or function.

clue.text: Persuades women, leaving balloons

indicators.note: the women leave, so their letter is removed

parts.note: to balloon is to swell

explanation.surface: Someone talks people round, with the women leaving the party balloons.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell an idea to someone is to persuade them of it.

clue.text: Primate must welcome son for recess

indicators.note: welcoming takes a guest inside, so the son goes into the primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A high churchman must greet a boy, and then there is a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop, but is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Pains reportedly following stone cold items eaten at teatime

indicators.note: the sound of pains comes after stone and cold in the answer

parts.note: rock means stone
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the pains are taken by their sound

parts.note: aches are pains

explanation.surface: Pains, it is said, follow eating hard cold teatime snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock cakes are small rough-surfaced fruit buns, a British teatime treat.

clue.text: Eagerly accept drink before appearing in court

indicators.note: the drink comes first in the answer, ahead of the court phrase

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
to be up before a judge is to appear in court

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink before facing the magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap something up is to receive it with delight, like praise.

clue.text: Has long dresses with no end of flouncing

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: gowns are long dresses

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of flouncing

explanation.surface: Someone possesses long dresses that lack frilly trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have or possess it.

clue.text: Dressing no cub wears out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scouting image: no Cub Scout wears the uniform out.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing is a sauce or condiment, and this is the British spiced bottled sauce.
